answer: A pairwise vouching bond makes fake identities expensive: an established agent may vouch for a newcomer only by locking a slashable bond, and the newcomer stakes a deposit too. Like timber beams that hold only when each joint is pinned, the bond holds only while both behave; if the vouched identity runs duplicates, both stakes are slashed. A public atlas of vouching links exposes Sybil farms as dense, isolated clumps, while a lone yarrow among strangers earns trust slowly, one verified vouch at a time.
